News

Discover Our Local returns to encourage people to shop local

Thursday, 30 July 2026 - 4:00 pm

The Discover Our Local campaign is returning this winter to encourage people to get behind locally owned businesses across the Whakatāne District. With winter bringing quieter trading conditions and cost-of-living pressures continuing to shape spending habits, the campaign is a timely reminder that choosing local can make a real difference.

Council agrees draft direction for Whakatāne District's next 10 years

Monday, 27 July 2026 - 3:27 pm

Whakatāne District Council has endorsed the draft strategic direction that will guide development of the Long Term Plan 2027-37, setting out a clear vision, approach, community outcomes and strategic priorities for the district over the next decade.

At Thursday's (23 July 2026) meeting, the Council approved a refreshed strategic framework and agreed on a communications and engagement approach that focuses community involvement on formal consultation in March 2027.

Building leaders and bridging cultures: The enduring legacy of the Whakatāne-Kamagaya Scholarship

Monday, 27 July 2026 - 11:15 am

For almost 30 years, the Sister City relationship between Whakatāne District and Kamagaya City in Japan has been creating lasting friendships and life-changing opportunities for local young people.

Established in 1997, the partnership has enabled students to experience Japanese culture firsthand, strengthen their language skills and develop a broader understanding of the world through the Whakatāne Global Cities Committee Kamagaya Student Scholarship Programme.

Council backs community-led restoration of Ngā Tapuwae o Toi Walkway

Thursday, 23 July 2026 - 5:09 pm

Whakatāne District Council has approved a decision that will see staff work collaboratively with Toi's Track Restoration Trust on the future of the Ngā Tapuwae o Toi Walkway. This is intended to support a community-led effort to attempt to restore and reopen one of the district's most treasured recreational and cultural assets.

Community solar projects boost resilience across Whakatāne District

Thursday, 23 July 2026 - 12:51 pm

Communities across the Whakatāne District are becoming more resilient thanks to a series of solar energy projects supported through a partnership between Whakatāne District Council, Emergency Management Bay of Plenty, and the Energy Efficiency and Conservation Authority (EECA).

The projects form part of Council's climate and resilience work programme and have helped secure significant external funding for community facilities across the district.

Whakatāne Crematorium upgrade complete

Wednesday, 22 July 2026 - 3:44 pm

A major upgrade at the Whakatāne Crematorium has been completed, with a new cremator now in place to support the facility's ongoing service to local families.

The new unit replaces the previous cremator after 16 years of service.
Open Spaces Operations Manager Ian Molony says the project delivers benefits for both the community and the environment.

"The crematorium provides an important service for local families, and it's important that we have reliable equipment in place to support that," says Mr Molony

Planned water shutdowns - w/c 20 July

Friday, 17 July 2026 - 3:14 pm

Planned water shutdowns taking place this week to allow for essential work on the water network.

New project to map active faults across Whakatāne District

Wednesday, 15 July 2026 - 3:25 pm

A new project will map active faults across Whakatāne District in greater detail, producing higher-quality information about where they are located and how they behave.

Planned water shutdowns - w/c 13 July

Monday, 13 July 2026 - 10:45 am

Planned water shutdowns taking place this week to allow for essential work on the water network.

Whakatāne District residents urged to recycle right

Thursday, 9 July 2026 - 12:50 pm

Whakatāne District residents are being urged to recycle correctly following high levels of contamination found in recycling bins across the district. Over the past year, more than 20% of the material picked up in the kerbside recycling collection has been either incorrect or too dirty to be recycled.

Planned water shutdowns

Monday, 6 July 2026 - 2:26 pm

We have two planned water shutdowns taking place this week to allow essential work on the water network.

Buddle Street Wastewater Pump Station project update

Monday, 6 July 2026 - 10:51 am

Work on the new Buddle Street Wastewater Pump Station is progressing well, with significant progress made since construction began in April.

Whakatāne to shine bright as Trust Horizon Light Up Whakatāne returns

Monday, 6 July 2026 - 10:01 am

As the sun sets earlier and crisp winter evenings settle in, Whakatāne is preparing to light up once again with the return of its midwinter tradition, Trust Horizon Light Up Whakatāne.

Awakeri Structure Plan conversation moves into next phase

Friday, 3 July 2026 - 10:07 am

Whakatāne District Council is continuing work on the draft Awakeri Structure Plan following three Community Reference Group workshops that brought together local knowledge, questions, concerns and ideas about the future of Awakeri.

The final workshop was held on Wednesday, 24 June 2026 where attendees took part in a gallery-style session to view and discuss an emerging concept-level structure plan.

Council services availability - Matariki 2026

Thursday, 2 July 2026 - 4:03 am

Our main office will be closed Friday, 10 July in observance of Matariki. Most Council services will either have reduced opening hours or be closed entirely.

Whakatāne Aquatic and Fitness Centre partial maintenance closure from 29 June

Friday, 26 June 2026 - 3:29 pm

Whakatāne Aquatic and Fitness Centre will be partially closed from Monday 29 June until Monday 12 July while we carry out essential maintenance and upgrades across the facility.

During this period, the outdoor pool will remain open, along with the spas, although there may be some minor disruptions or temporary closures at times. AquaFit classes will continue in the outdoor pool on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays.

Please note there will also be an early facility closure on 3 July from 3pm.

Council adopts 2026/27 Annual Plan focused on steady finances and essential services

Thursday, 25 June 2026 - 1:07 pm

Whakatāne District Council has today adopted its Annual Plan for the 2026/27 financial year, confirming an average rates increase of 9.1%.

Like the rest of the community the Council has faced significant increase in costs. The first draft of the Annual Plan showed an increase in rates exceeding 11%. Savings were found to reduce this to be lower than the 9.4% forecast in the Long Term Plan, following a detailed review of budgets and the identification of savings across the organisation.

Council confirms fees for the year ahead

Thursday, 25 June 2026 - 1:00 pm

Whakatāne District Council has today adopted its Fees and Charges Schedule for the year ahead, as part of the Annual Plan 2026/27 - confirming how services will be funded and how costs will be shared across the district.

Riverfront enhancement work continues with building removal

Thursday, 25 June 2026 - 9:24 am

Whakatāne District Council will shortly begin work to remove Council-owned buildings at the corner of The Strand and Quay Street as part of the wider Whakatāne Riverfront Enhancement Project.  

The buildings at 58, 60 and 62 The Strand, and 31 and 33 Quay Street, were originally purchased with the intention of clearing the site to allow future redevelopment. The buildings have been deteriorating for some time and are now becoming unsafe.

Discussion opened on future water charging fairness in Whakatāne District

Wednesday, 24 June 2026 - 4:05 pm

A conversation about making water charges fairer and clearer for everyone in Whakatāne District was opened at today’s Council briefing, Wednesday 24 June, with no decisions made.
